name: Ciprofloxacin
summary: Fluoroquinolone with potent Gram-negative and antipseudomonal activity; key oral option for prostatitis and GI pathogens.
mechanism: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication.
pharmacodynamics: Concentration-dependent killing with a post-antibiotic effect.

dosing.adult: 500 mg PO every 12 hours (400 mg IV every 12 hours) for UTI/respiratory/skin infections

safety.pregnancy: Generally avoided (cartilage toxicity in animal studies)
warnings: Tendon rupture (risk increased by age and corticosteroids)
CNS effects (seizures, confusion); caution in myasthenia gravis

clinicalPearls: Chelates divalent cations (Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, antacids) — separate dosing by 2+ hours
Potent oral antipseudomonal, but weak against S. pneumoniae compared with levofloxacin
good: Oral antipseudomonal with excellent prostate and GI pathogen penetration.
bad: Tendon rupture, QT, and dysglycemia risks; high E. coli resistance limits empiric UTI use in many regions.
